metadata.description: TERA eligibility criteria for military members retiring with 15-20 years of service

program_overview.name: Temporary Early Retirement Authority (TERA)
program_overview.purpose: Provides temporary authority for voluntary early retirement of eligible service members with 15-20 years of active service
program_overview.note: TERA retirees receive 2.5% per year of service (same as normal retirement), but with fewer years results in lower monthly pension

basic_requirements.description: Must be serving on active duty at time of retirement
Minimum 15 years, maximum less than 20 years of creditable active service
Requires approval from Secretary of the military department
Service member must voluntarily apply for TERA retirement
TERA program must be active and available for member's branch
basic_requirements.note: TERA availability varies by service branch and force structure requirements

additional_requirements: Must be in approved MOS/grade combination
Army.notes: Army typically opens TERA windows annually based on force management needs

additional_requirements: Must be in approved rating/grade combination
Navy.notes: Navy TERA availability varies by rating and paygrade

additional_requirements: Must be in approved AFSC/grade combination
Air Force.notes: Air Force typically offers TERA during force reduction initiatives

additional_requirements: Must be in approved MOS/grade combination
Marine Corps.notes: Marine Corps TERA windows are often limited and selective

Space Force.notes: TERA not currently available for Space Force members due to force building phase

Coast Guard.notes: Coast Guard typically does not offer TERA; uses other separation programs

disqualifying_factors.description: General Court-Martial conviction typically disqualifies TERA eligibility
disqualifying_factors.exceptions: Case-by-case basis depending on nature of offense

disqualifying_factors.description: Member under investigation or pending court-martial
disqualifying_factors.exceptions: May be eligible after resolution if otherwise qualified
Some commitments may be waived for TERA purposes

disqualifying_factors.description: Members eligible for medical retirement typically processed under disability system instead
disqualifying_factors.exceptions: May elect TERA in lieu of disability retirement in some cases

retirement_calculation.high_36_definition: Average of highest 36 months of basic pay

benefits.description: Begin receiving retirement pay upon retirement
benefits.note: No waiting period; payments start upon retirement date

benefits.description: Access to TRICARE health insurance for retiree and dependents
Eligible for VA healthcare, disability compensation, and other VA programs
Continued access to military shopping facilities

limitations.description: TERA retirement results in significantly lower monthly pension compared to 20-year retirement
limitations.impact: At 15 years: 37.5% vs 50% at 20 years (25% less income)

limitations.description: Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) deduction is higher percentage of smaller retirement pay
limitations.note: SBP costs same % but applies to lower base amount

limitations.description: Annual Cost of Living Adjustments (COLA) apply to smaller base amount
limitations.impact: Lower starting pension means lower cumulative COLA increases over lifetime

limitations.description: Once retired under TERA, cannot return to active duty to complete 20 years
limitations.note: Decision is permanent; cannot reverse to complete full 20-year career

limitations.description: TERA retirement pay NOT subject to Redux recalculation at age 62
limitations.note: This is actually beneficial - no reduction at age 62 for TERA retirees

steps.description: Watch for TERA application windows announced by service branch
steps.timeline: Varies by service; typically annual or as needed

steps.description: Confirm years of service, grade, MOS/rating eligibility
Complete and submit TERA retirement application through chain of command
Attend pre-separation counseling and financial planning sessions
Service Secretary reviews and approves/disapproves applications
If approved, receive retirement orders with effective date
Final day of active service; retirement effective

financial: Calculate lifetime retirement income difference (15-19 years vs 20 years)
Compare TERA retirement to civilian earning potential
Factor in healthcare costs (TRICARE vs civilian insurance)
Consider Survivor Benefit Plan (SBP) costs and coverage
Evaluate impact on TSP/401k savings timeline
healthcare: TRICARE coverage for retirees and dependents
Compare costs: TRICARE vs civilian employer insurance
career: Civilian job market for your skills
Certifications and education needed for civilian career

official.description: Official retirement pay information and calculators

calculators.description: Compare active duty pay vs retirement scenarios
